name: Sika MultiSeal BT
paste:
SIKA® MULTISEAL BT: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® MultiSeal BT, April 2026, Version 04.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sika-multiseal-bt.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® MultiSeal BT where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2026, Version 04.01).
1.2 Product description. Sika® MultiSeal BT is a self-adhesive sealing tape based on a butyl rubber compound reinforced with an aluminium film. High tack butyl adhesive ensures reliable, durable long term bonding to a wide range of substrates in internal and external applications.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. The Sika® MultiSeal BT is used for repairing, protecting and sealing:
    - Sheet metal roofs
    - Facade elements
    - Concrete roof tiles
    - Gutters and down pipes in metal and PVC
    - Chimneys and sky lights
    - Caravans and containers
    - Modular buildings and office containers
    - Ductwork for ventilation and air condition
    - Dampening and insulation
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.6.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® MultiSeal BT
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: HIGH TACK ELASTOMERIC BUTYL SEALING TAPE
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2026, Version 04.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ASTM D 792: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.1).
    - EN 1849-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Thickness (p.2).
    - ASTM D 1000: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Adhesion in peel (p.2); Technical Information > Elongation (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Fast and easy installation
    - Good adhesion at low temperatures
    - Wide service temperature range
    - Good adhesion to many construction materials
    - Very good resistance to weathering and UV
    - Very good dimensional stability
    - Very good heat stability, no flow and oil migration
    - Flexible
    - High strength
    - Can be painted with most conventional paints*
    * Sika® MultiSeal BT can be overpainted with most conventional paint systems. However, paints must first be tested to ensure compatibility by carrying out preliminary trials.
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Butyl rubber compound
    - Colour: Grey
    - Density: ~1.5g/cm³ (ASTM D 792)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Top surface: Aluminium foil
    - Bottom surface: Self adhesive butyl rubber compound protected with a release liner
    - Tensile strength: ~ 120 (N/25mm) (ASTM D 1000)
    - Elongation: ~80% (ASTM D 1000)
    - Resistance to UV exposure: The film provides UV resistance
    - Adhesion in peel: ≥20 on steel (180° peel, N/25mm) (ASTM D 1000)
2.7 Service temperature.
    | Maximum | +80 °C |
    | Minimum | -30 °C |
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 36 months from date of production
2.9 Packaging.
    | Length per roll | Tape width | Rolls per box |
    | 10 m | 100 mm | 3 |
2.10 Storage conditions. The Product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +25 °C. Always refer to packaging. Refer to the current Safety Data Sheet for information on safe handling and storage.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2026, Version 04.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be sound, clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, cement laitance, old sealants and poorly bonded coatings which could affect adhesion of the tape. The substrate must be of sufficient strength to cope with the stresses induced by the tape during movement.
    - For optimal adhesion, the following procedure is recommended.
3.3 Non-porous substrates. Clean and pre-treat the substrate with Sika® Aktivator- 205 applied with a clean towel. Allow a flash-off time > 10 min (max. 2 hours) before applying the tape.
3.4 Porous substrates. Use hot air to pre-heat concrete, aerated concrete and cementitious plasters, mortars and brick substrates to increase adhesion.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2026, Version 04.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Thickness: Including film 1.0 mm (EN 1849-1)
4.3 Application method / tools. Cut the tape to required length, remove the release liner and press the tape firmly onto the prepared substrate with a hard wheel roller or suitable tool. All joints and connections must be overlapped by a minimum of 50mm. Low temperatures can reduce adhesion, warm the tape and substrate using a hot air blower for a few minutes prior to application.
4.4 Overpainting the tape. The top aluminium film side of the Product can be overpainted with most conventional paint coating systems. Do not use solvent-based paints. Test the compatability of the paint coating with the Product before application.
4.5 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after use with petroleum or turpentine. Once cured, hardened material can only be removed mechanically. For cleaning skin use Sika® Cleaning Wipes-100 and wash with water and soap.
4.6 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not use on natural stone substrates.
    - Due to the chemical content of the tape, coatings and plastics may discolour, test for compatability prior to any use.
    - Not suitable for sealing against water pressure.
    - Not suitable as a permanent fixing and in load bearing applications.
    - Not suitable for permanently immersed applications.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Butyl adhesives are sensitive to solvents, check for chemical compatability befor use.
    - On porous substrates, water infiltration underneath the tape is possible which may affect adhesion. Thoroughly dry out substrates before applying the Product. Plasticiser migration from the Product may result in reduced adhesion, surface discolouration, or surface tackiness. Test the compatibility of the Product with the substrate before application.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature.
    | Maximum | +45 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
5.3 Substrate temperature.
    | Maximum | +45 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
5.4 Substrate moisture content. The substrates must be dry
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: ~1.5g/cm³ (ASTM D 792)
    - Thickness: Including film 1.0 mm (EN 1849-1)
    - Tensile strength: ~ 120 (N/25mm) (ASTM D 1000)
    - Elongation: ~80% (ASTM D 1000)
    - Adhesion in peel: ≥20 on steel (180° peel, N/25mm) (ASTM D 1000)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® MultiSeal BT, April 2026, Version 04.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sika-multiseal-bt.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® MultiSeal-BT, version 28/07/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sds-sika-multiseal-bt.pdf
    - Document: Sika MultiSeal-BT AP SDS, https://aus.sika.com/dms/getdocument.get/77573b1f-d768-33d1-a86d-f38298c14635/SIKA%20MULTISEAL%20BT%20AP%20SDS.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. This product is an article as defined in article 3 of regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH). It contains no substances which are intended to be released from the article under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use. A safety data sheet following article 31 of the same regulation is not needed to bring the product to the market, to transport or to use it. For safe use follow the instructions given in the product data sheet. Based on our current knowledge, this product does not contain SVHC (substances of very high concern) as listed in Annex XIV of the REACH regulation or on the candidate list published by the European Chemicals Agency in concentrations above 0,1 % (w/w).
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
